metadata.scenario: A patient calls urgently requesting to speak to a therapist about an unusual reaction following a therapy session. Category: Urgent Request. Flags: urgent_request.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret, how can I help you today? Hi Margaret, this is Robert Jackson. I need to speak to someone urgently about my therapy session. Of course, Robert. What's going on? I had a session with Dr. Rodriguez a few days ago, and since then, I've been feeling really strange—dizziness and some nausea. I’m so sorry to hear that. Let me get you in touch with Dr. Rodriguez right away. That would be great. I’m really worried—this isn’t like me. I understand. Can you confirm your last visit date? It was three days ago, on Tuesday. Thank you. I’ll call Dr. Rodriguez to see if he can speak with you. Please hold for just a moment. Okay, I’ll wait. (after a brief hold) Robert, I’ve reached Dr. Rodriguez. He’s currently with another patient but will return your call within the hour. Is that okay? Yes, that’s fine. I just hope it’s nothing serious. I understand your concern, and he’ll be able to address that. Are you experiencing any other symptoms? No, just the dizziness and nausea. Thank you for clarifying. I’ll make sure he knows that when he calls back. Appreciate it. Also, I was wondering if I could add some companion care to my schedule? Certainly! We can look into that. Do you have specific days in mind? Maybe just a few hours a week? I could use some help with errands. We can certainly arrange that. I'll connect you with our Care Coordinator, Lisa, after your call with Dr. Rodriguez. Sounds good, thank you! You're welcome! Is there anything else you’d like to discuss while I have you on the line? No, that’s it for now. Alright, Robert. I’ll ensure Dr. Rodriguez calls you shortly. Thank you, Margaret. I appreciate your help. You’re very welcome. Take care, and we’ll be in touch soon. Bye. Goodbye.
